content.text: I have inspected all fee, termination, liability, indemnity, and general provisions. No Customer-payable liquidated damages, penalty, or early-termination charge exists anywhere.

input.quote: Sparkling may terminate this Agreement at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice to Garman. If Sparkling terminates this Agreement pursuant to this Section 17(b), Sparkling shall cease using the Software at the end of the ninety (90) day notice period, and shall certify to Garman within thirty (30) calendar days of termination that Sparkling has destroyed or has returned to Garman all Software, Documentation and Codes.
input.rationale: The Agreement imposes no liquidated damages, penalty, stipulated-damages or minimum-fee obligation on Sparkling. Section 11 (p0084) obliges Sparkling only to pay the fees set out in the Fee Schedule; Section 17(b) (p0118) lets Sparkling terminate on 90 days' notice with no termination charge or accelerated/remaining-term payment; and Section 17(c) (p0128) runs in our favour on Garman default (perpetual licence plus refund of prepaid fees). Section 15 (p0105) is a mutual damages limitation, not a stipulated-damages mechanic, and the only reference to "penalties" (p0090) is within Garman's IP indemnity in our favour. This therefore satisfies the preferred position that Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties, and no redline is warranted. We note only for completeness that the Fee Schedule (Schedule "A") is not reproduced in the reviewed text, so any stipulated early-termination or minimum-fee amount appearing there should be confirmed as absent.
